title: A teacher had an empty classroom and a ‘crazy idea.’ Lowe’s answered her letter
summary: A teacher had an empty classroom and a ‘crazy idea.’ Lowe’s answered her letter
body_markdown:
For Houser, the additions are about more than filling an empty room.


With designated places for computers,


supplies


and materials, her second graders can navigate the classroom with more independence.


“Just having places that are organized,


that


they know where to go in the classroom gives them some ownership of the classroom,” Houser said.


Principal Chad Dennison sees something bigger in what happened.


Rossville is a small, rural community where students from pre-K through 12th grade share one school complex. To Dennison, the response showed what can happen when someone sees a need and acts.


“You have someone at the highest level you


can have


get something from someone who lives in a small rural town in Indiana and


say


, ‘Hey, there’s a need out there. And if we can help, let’s


help,’”


Dennison said.


For Houser, that response still resonates.


“So many times we write letters


maybe


asking for help, and they go unanswered,” she said. “But to know that he saw my letter, reached out to someone who contacted me and said, ‘Hey, we want to help you’ … I am so thankful.”


Her once-empty classroom now has places for students to sit, learn,


organize


and make the space their own.


And Houser’s “crazy idea” left her with something else.


“I know what kind of people work for Lowe’s,” she said. “And I love that because they were so kind to me.”
